summary_en: Full-year dividend for fiscal year ending March 2027 raised by 10 yen per share to 55 yen at fiscal year-end, bringing total annual dividend to 85 yen, up 30 yen from prior year. Earnings forecast also upgraded across all metrics due to stronger-than-expected student enrollment and summer program revenue, coupled with cost efficiencies.
title_en: Notice of Revision of Business Forecast and Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Waseda Academy has revised its dividend forecast for fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The company increased the year-end dividend by 10 yen per share from the previously announced 45 yen to 55 yen, resulting in a total annual dividend of 85 yen. This represents a 30 yen increase compared to the prior fiscal year's 55 yen in total dividends (20 yen interim plus 35 yen year-end).

The dividend increase follows an upward revision of the company's full-year earnings forecast. Revenue is now expected to reach 40.9 billion yen (up from 40.52 billion yen), operating profit 4.77 billion yen (up from 4.239 billion yen), and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders 3.08 billion yen (up from 2.752 billion yen). The company attributed the improved performance to stronger-than-expected student enrollment and robust revenue from summer programs and intensive training courses in the first half of the fiscal year.

On the cost side, the company deferred some advertising, digital transformation, and capital expenditures to the second half, while benefiting from improved operational efficiency as the number of students per school location increased. The company stated that dividends are a key component of shareholder returns and aims to maintain a dividend payout ratio of 50% or higher in line with its medium-term management plan.
